items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 48:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the lower beard of AA? The hairs of the beard of AA in their entirety are divided into three aspects: MEM-LAMED-TZADIK, in the manner that the Mochin of AB are divided in the three ascents of ZA, as is said below in Answers 68 and 69. Whereby the eight upper corrections of the beard, which hang from the cheeks of the head of AA, are the aspect of the MEM of the Tzelem and KHB. And the four lower corrections, which hang from the throat, are the aspect of the LAMED and HGT. And the hairs that are in the Yesod of AA are the aspect of the TZADIK and NHY, and are called the lower beard of AA. And it is known that all these Mochin that come out upon the hairs of the beard, AA himself has no need of them, being the aspect of the Hochma of the direct light. Rather, they are divided between Aba and Ima and the ZON, for the aspect of the MEM-LAMED of the hairs of the beard, which are the two Mazalot, are taken by Aba and Ima, and the aspect of the TZADIK of the hairs, which is the lower beard, is taken by ZA, being the aspect of the NHY of Keter, as is known. In this manner, all the thirteen corrections of the beard of ZA come from the lower beard of AA. And although ZA has the thirteen corrections of the beard only at his ascent to the GAR of AA, nevertheless the ladder of degrees never changes, for at the time ZA ascends to the GAR of AA, the GAR of AA themselves are already found to have ascended to the AB of AK, and their NHY with ZA are found in the place of the GAR of AA from the aspect of permanence. Behold, that even at ZA's ascent to the GAR of AA, he still clothes upon the Yesod of AA as in his first degree, and therefore he receives the thirteen upper corrections only from the aspect of the Yesod of AA, which is from his lower beard. (Item 110).
